findings.title: Node.js October 2026 Security Releases (vendor advisory)
findings.summary_md: Node.js released security updates for supported lines on 21 October 2026, disclosing a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497) that permits remote code execution when applications decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data.

findings.title: Node2Shell: From Brotli Data to Remote Code Execution (Imperva)
findings.summary_md: Imperva's red team demonstrated working remote code execution against an official vulnerable Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 build using crafted Brotli data, confirming CVE-2026-111497 is exploitable in practice and that fixed releases correctly reject the malicious payload.

findings.title: Brandefense analysis naming HTTP2Shell and tracking CVE-2026-111497
findings.summary_md: Brandefense notes the Brotli decoder flaw began circulating under the name HTTP2Shell late on 23 October 2026 (UTC). The same CVE-2026-111497 affects both Node.js and Python Brotli packages (brotlicffi), expanding exposure beyond Node.js alone.
